detail: 90 readings reported in order with correct temperatures
finalText:
## Root cause

The queue carried `char *` pointers, but `sensor_task` had a **single stack buffer `line`** that it overwrote on every iteration:

```c
char line[48];
...
snprintf(line, ...);      // same buffer reused each reading
char *msg = line;
xQueueSend(readings, &msg, ...);   // only the address is queued
```

Because `sensor_task` has higher priority than `report_task`, it fills the whole 5-reading burst before the reporter drains anything. All five queued pointers therefore alias the *same* memory, which by then holds only the last reading of the burst. The reporter then printed that one reading five times. Observed on the board:

```
report seq=4 temp=21.48   (x5)
report seq=9 temp=20.33   (x5)
report seq=14 temp=22.18  (x5)
```

So each burst appeared as its last sample repeated, and all earlier samples were silently lost.

## Fix (`main/main.c`)

Made the queue carry the reading **by value** instead of by pointer:

- Added `typedef struct { char text[LINE_LEN]; } reading_msg_t;`
- `sensor_task` formats into a local `reading_msg_t msg` and sends `&msg`; `xQueueSend` copies the contents into the queue slot.
- `report_task` receives into its own `reading_msg_t msg` and prints `msg.text`.
- Queue created with `sizeof(reading_msg_t)`.

Burst size (5), burst interval (500 ms), and the `report seq=<n> temp=<t>` line format are unchanged.

## Verification

After flashing, the board prints every reading exactly once, strictly in order with distinct temperatures:

```
report seq=0 temp=20.00
report seq=1 temp=20.37
report seq=2 temp=20.74
...
```

A second capture showed 60 consecutive lines, seq 0–59 with no gaps and no `queue full` drops.
